message.content:
{
  "screen_decision": "include",
  "screen_rationale": "The study uses patient-derived tumor xenografts (PDXs) in mice to predict clinical trial drug response, reporting quantitative measures of concordance between PDX responses and clinical outcomes for various treatments. It explicitly compares PDX responses to clinical data to assess translatability.",
  "arm": "efficacy",
  "arm_evidence": "We demonstrate both the reproducibility and the clinical translatability of this approach by identifying associations between a genotype and drug response, and established mechanisms of resistance.",
  "therapeutic_areas": [
    "oncology"
  ],
  "areas_evidence": "High-throughput screening using patient-derived tumor xenografts to predict clinical trial drug response",
  "model_type": "xenograft-pdx",
  "model_evidence": "We established ~1,000 patient-derived tumor xenograft models (PDXs) with a diverse set of driver mutations.",
  "species": [
    "mouse"
  ],
  "species_evidence": "Patient tumor material was collected in culture medium and kept on wet ice for engraftment within 24 h after resection. ... Approximately 20–30-mg tissue fragments were implanted subcutaneously into the flank region of athymic nude (nu/nu) female mice using a trocar.",
  "endpoint_class": "mixed",
  "endpoint_evidence": "The response was determined by comparing tumor volume change at time t to its baseline: % tumor volume change = ∆Volt = 100% × ((Vt – Vinitial) / Vinitial). The BestResponse was the minimum value of ∆Volt for t ≥ 10 d. ... mCR, BestResponse < −95% and BestAvgResponse < −40%; mPR, BestResponse < −50% and BestAvgResponse < −20%; mSD, BestResponse < 35% and BestAvgResponse < 30%; mPD, not otherwise categorized."
}
